title: Find the point after the turn
hook: The main idea covers the whole text. It usually comes right after 'but,' 'however,' or 'instead.'

steps.prompt: Try this first. 'Brandt expected gardens with the most flower species to draw the most pollinators. Instead, visits depended mainly on how close a garden was to a park.' Main idea:
choices: Pollinators avoid gardens with many species.
Brandt found location mattered more than flower variety.
Gardens usually have more species than parks.
steps.why: Instead marks the finding. The main idea is what Brandt found, not what she expected.

steps.prompt: Sort each choice for that text.

cards.text: Brandt studied gardens in three cities.
All insects prefer parks to gardens.
A garden's location mattered more than its variety of flowers.

steps.why: Too narrow: a true detail that isn't the point. Too broad: a claim the text never makes. Just right covers the whole text.

steps.prompt: Why is the sentence after a turn word so important?
steps.answer: Texts often set up an expectation or common view, then turn. The author's real point comes after the turn.

steps.prompt: Read fast. Then: which turn word was NOT in the list?
steps.why: For example adds support; it doesn't turn. The others all signal that the main point is coming.

steps.prompt: 'Economists assumed lottery winners stop working. But a study found most kept their jobs, cutting hours only slightly.' Main idea:
choices: The study challenges the assumption that winners usually stop working.
Winners in the study earned less over time.
Most economists now agree winners work more.
steps.why: The turn word 'But' introduces the study that challenges the assumption.

steps.prompt: Which choice is the classic trap on main idea questions?
choices: A true detail from one sentence
A choice that covers the whole text
A choice that uses the author's claim
steps.why: A true but narrow detail is the most common wrong answer.

keys: The main idea covers the whole text, not one detail.
Look for the turn: but, however, instead, yet, in fact.
Reject choices that are too narrow, too broad, or compare things the text never compares.

recall.prompt: The most common wrong answer on main idea questions is:
choices: a true detail that's too narrow
a summary of the whole text
recall.why: Narrow details tempt you because they're true.

recall.prompt: Where does the author's point usually appear?

recall.answer: However, but, instead (also yet, in fact).
